name: PA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 15 points on the partisan baseline
Scanlon is a well-funded incumbent with a large cash advantage
Challenger Manganaro has raised under $10,000, leaving him unable to compete
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 98%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Scanlon: a +15 Democratic district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge against a challenger with minimal resources. Markets and the structural picture agree this is not competitive.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention on the Republican side, or a dramatic national shift toward the GOP, would be the main things to watch.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon (D) is running.

overview:
Mary Gay Scanlon seeks another term in a Delaware County district that leans Democratic by about 15 points. She enters the race with roughly $450,000 on hand after raising nearly $1 million, while Republican Nicholas Manganaro has raised under $10,000 and has no meaningful outside support. No independent groups are spending against the incumbent.

With no public polling of the race and no expert raters flagging it as competitive, the outlook rests on fundamentals, which all point one direction. Prediction markets price the Democrat at about 98%, consistent with a comfortable double-digit expected margin and only a small chance of an upset.
